sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: The Orissa Famine (1866) killed nearly 1/3rd of the population, exposing the failure of the **Laissez-faire** policy of the British administration.
• **Mandate**: Sir George Campbell was appointed to investigate the causes of the famine and recommend measures to prevent future occurrences.
• **Core Philosophy**: The commission emphasized the need for **State intervention** in food supply and the necessity of maintaining **Famine Relief Works**.
• **Key Metric**: The commission highlighted the lack of **transport infrastructure** (railways/roads) as a primary reason for the inability to move food grains to affected regions.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Affected Orissa, Bihar, and Bengal; high mortality due to administrative apathy.
Failure of monsoon + export of food grains + lack of transport.
Prelims: Trigger for the first Famine Commission.
First formal inquiry into famine management in British India.
Shift from 'charity' to 'state duty' in famine relief.

items.definition: The economic doctrine of non-interference by the government. The commission challenged this by proving that market forces alone could not prevent mass starvation.
A set of administrative guidelines for relief operations, which eventually evolved from the recommendations of the Campbell and subsequent commissions.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Infrastructure Development**: Prioritization of irrigation and railway connectivity to ensure food security.
• **Data Collection**: Systematic recording of crop failure and mortality rates to inform future policy.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Colonial priority remained on revenue collection over human welfare.
• **Solutions**: Subsequent commissions (Strachey, Lyall) refined the relief mechanisms into a more structured 'Famine Code'.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'C-O-R' (Campbell - Orissa - Relief).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Campbell Commission was the first to address the Orissa famine and initiate the concept of state-led relief.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Campbell Commission (1866) with the Strachey Commission (1880). Remember: Campbell was the FIRST (1866), Strachey was the most comprehensive (1880).
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'From Administrative Apathy to Institutionalized Relief' to describe the evolution of British famine policy.

keyTakeaways: The Campbell Commission was the first formal recognition of the state's responsibility in famine management.
It identified the lack of transport and infrastructure as the critical bottleneck in food distribution.
It laid the conceptual groundwork for the later, more robust Famine Codes of the 1880s.
